front_question: Define parity of integers and give algebraic representations for even and odd numbers.
back_answer: Parity is the property of an integer being even or odd. Any even number is 2n; any odd number is 2n - 1 (or 2n + 1) for an integer n.

front_question: State the parity rules for addition and multiplication of even and odd numbers.
back_answer: Addition: Even + Even = Even; Odd + Odd = Even; Even + Odd = Odd. Multiplication: Even * Anything = Even; Odd * Odd = Odd.

front_question: Why is the sum of page numbers on any single loose sheet torn from a book always odd?
back_answer: A two-sided leaf has front page 2k-1 (odd) and back page 2k (even). Their sum = (2k-1) + 2k = 4k - 1, which is always an odd integer.

front_question: Prove why the center cell of a 3x3 magic square filled with numbers 1 to 9 must equal 5.
back_answer: Sum of 1 to 9 = 45; row sum = 45 / 3 = 15. The center cell x belongs to 4 lines (row 2, col 2, two diagonals). Summing all 4 lines gives 4 * 15 = 60. In this sum, every cell is counted once, except x which is counted 4 times: 45 + 3x = 60 => 3x = 15 => x = 5.
